critique: The render has the intended black backdrop, bright yellow/orange/red ember palette, dense emission, and a discernible downward shift from t1 to t4. However, it still reads as a narrow central column of soft bead-like particles rather than the broader, scattered falling-sparks shower of the preset thumbnail. The lateral field is too constrained and the visible trail remains relatively compact, with the lower portion crowding/cropping near the bottom instead of sustaining a more extended descending shower.

suggestions.why: Substantially widening the line emitter spreads the source across more of the frame, breaking the tight centered column.
A wider direction spread disperses sparks laterally after emission, creating a more natural shower rather than a vertically packed plume.
Longer particle life preserves a longer descending field and makes the falling motion read more clearly across the frame.
